claims.text: All three transactional artifacts describe the same trip, which discharges the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) before any threshold is reached: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-09112, and the gps_trace's first fix (2026-09-19T14:10:00+08:00) matches the trip_record's started_at to the second, so the trace the rider measures against is the trace of this trip and not of some other job.

On the measurement POL-RD-01 makes governing, the trip is longer than the route shown at booking. POL-RD-01 fixes gps_trace.trace_distance_km as the governing field and forbids citing the trip_record's rounded copy of the same measurement for the threshold test; the trace reads 11.5 km against a booking-time optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km. The absolute limb of the POL-RD-01 test (greater than 0.8 km) is satisfied at almost twice the required margin.

The 1.5 km is not a sampling artefact and nothing justifies discounting it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum interval gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not engaged at all and the measurement stands at the artifact's full admissibility weight of 1.0 rather than being down-weighted under POL-GEN-02.

The additional distance was not asked for by the rider, so the driver cannot lay it at the rider's door. The chat log for this trip holds exactly one message, sent by the rider at 14:21:40, reading 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking.'; its waypoint_hint is null and no road or place is named. Under POL-RD-04 no rider instruction is recorded, no waypoint can be tested, and no part of the excess is excluded as rider-requested.

No external event explains the excess either, and the rider discloses the state of the one artifact that could have. EV-ADVIS-09112-01, the traffic advisory slot for this route and window, is MISSING: it carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, weight 0.0 and no payload. Its absence is itself citable, and it establishes that no advisory covers the booked route and trip window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no closure, contraflow or junction works excuse any part of the 1.5 km. The rider relies on this artifact only for its absence and not for any positive fact.

The baseline the rider measures against is the correct one and nothing in the record shifts it. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booking-time optimal of 10.0 km stands as the only baseline in play.

The rider's profile gives the tribunal no ground to demand corroboration beyond the trace: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 rider-side trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and the extra-corroboration requirement is not engaged. The rider's remaining counters — prior_no_show_flags 1, prior_disputes_filed 1, prior_disputes_upheld 0 — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not carry any finding against the rider.

The driver's counter-statement that he 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' names no artifact and no clause, and the in-trip chat log records no driver message at all. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, so nothing in the bundle contradicts the 1.5 km excess measured on the trace.

If the excess is treated as established, the remedy is arithmetic and the rider's claimed SGD 1.69 is exactly it: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 20.0 optimal min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown, which is the only artifact carrying that field) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo discount = 17.70. Refund = 19.39 charged_total - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to SGD 1.70. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 8.72% of charged_total, so the outcome would be PARTIAL_REFUND and not a full refund; and with erp_gantries empty and off-route ERP totalling 0.00 there is no pass-through line to add on top under POL-RD-09.

The rider does not contend that the measured excess clears POL-RD-01 as written: 1.5 km is 15.0% of the 10.0 km optimal, short of the 20% limb, and both limbs must pass. The rider's submission is that the excess is nonetheless real, measured on an unimpaired trace, and unexplained by anything in the bundle — no rider instruction, no amendment, no closure, and the sole explanatory artifact EV-ADVIS-09112-01 missing (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0). On that record the rider asks that, if the tribunal does not apply the POL-RD-02 arithmetic above, the contested SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than left standing as collected, because the gap in the record is a data failure and not a finding that the extra distance was properly chargeable.

claims.text: The measured excess on this trip is 1.5 km against a 10.0 km optimal route — 15.00% of optimal, as derived in code from the trace itself (derived.deviation.excess_pct). POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km; 15.00% is below the 20% gate, so no deviation is established and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01's two limbs are conjunctive, not alternative. The absolute limb is met — 1.5 km is above the 0.8 km threshold_km — but the clause requires BOTH tests to pass, and states expressly that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's '1.5 km longer' is therefore not a deviation in policy terms; it is an excess that fails the percentage limb by 5 points.

There is no distance-field disagreement for the rider to exploit: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.5 km, which is the governing field under POL-RD-01, and the trip_record's actual_distance_km is the same 11.5 km — a rounded convenience copy. Use the governing figure and the excess is still 1.5 km / 15.00%.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired or incomplete: it carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, and its admissibility is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The rider therefore cannot route around the threshold via POL-RD-07, and the no-corroboration escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The initial burden under POL-RD-08 sits with the rider: she must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. On the unimpaired trace the excess is 15.00%, short of the 20% gate, so the burden is never discharged and the driver is never called on to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12.

The optimal distance is the platform's stored booking estimate — the routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot at 10.0 km — which is the figure POL-RD-01 directs be used. No relocation re-quote applies: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not disturb the baseline and the 20% gate remains 2.0 km, which the 1.5 km excess cannot reach.

The one refund route that survives a failed POL-RD-01 test — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — is closed on this record. The fare breakdown charges no ERP gantries (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.0) and applies no airport surcharge (0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport), so there is no phantom line to refund in full regardless of deviation.

No repeat-pattern uplift or conduct referral is available against the driver. POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, and a 15.00% excess of 1.5 km is neither greater than 50% of optimal nor greater than 8.0 km. In any event the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 — nowhere near the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test — so the citable profile fields add nothing against him.

The chat log does not carry the rider's case either. The sole message is her own mid-trip remark that the trip 'looks a little longer'; it names no place and no road and carries a null waypoint_hint, so under POL-RD-04 it neither records a rider-requested detour nor corroborates any excess, and the requirement to use the waypoint_hint field rather than geocode a place name means the corroboration test cannot be run at all. The driver's account — ordinary through roads, no additional stop — stands unrebutted.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this dispute turns entirely on the route-deviation threshold in POL-RD-01, and on that test the claim does not succeed.

THE MEASUREMENT. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, and the trip_record's actual_distance_km a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace (EV-GPS-09112) reads 11.5 km; the booking-time optimal route stored on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09112) is 10.0 km. The excess is 1.5 km, or 15.00% of the optimal distance.

THE TEST. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The 1.5 km excess clears the absolute limb (0.8 km) but fails the percentage limb: 15.00% is below 20%. Both limbs must pass, and the clause says in terms that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The deviation is therefore not established on this trip.

RIDER. Your submission that the 1.5 km is real and measured on an unimpaired trace is accepted: the trace carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and POL-GEN-02 gives no discount. But a real, unimpaired excess that does not clear both threshold limbs is simply not a deviation under this policy, and your own final submission concedes the percentage limb is short.

Your conditional POL-RD-02 arithmetic (recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 20.0) x surge 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 = 17.70; refund = 19.39 charged_total - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70) is answered but does not run: POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and it is not. Your alternative request to hold the SGD 1.69 for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 is refused because no POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match TRP-09112; the trace is not impaired; the timestamps agree; and there is no admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength between the parties. The billing-integrity route under POL-RD-09(4) is also closed on this record: erp_gantries is empty, tolls/ERP are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom line to refund in full.

DRIVER. Your counter-statement that you 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' cites no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; it is not relied on, and the ruling does not need it. The traffic-advisory slot EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so no closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 was available to you either — but since no deviation is established, none is needed.

OUTCOME. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence at the threshold the policy sets, so the present state stands: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 are left as they are, and the SGD 1.69 is neither refunded nor held. No clause produces a referral here: POL-RD-06(c) is not engaged (there is no MATERIAL deviation and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days), and there is no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4).

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is NO_ACTION: the fare of SGD 19.39 stands, no refund issues to the rider and no payment is due to the driver.

The reason is the threshold in POL-RD-01. On the governing field — gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 11.5 km — measured against the platform's booking-time optimal of 10.0 km (the routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot on the trip record), the excess is 1.5 km, or 15.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The absolute limb passes (1.5 km > 0.8 km) but the percentage limb fails: 15.0% is short of 20%, and 1.5 km is short of the 2.0 km that 20% of 10.0 km requires. Both limbs must pass, so no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The trip_record's actual_distance_km (11.5 km) is the same reading as the trace, so there is no distance-field disagreement to exploit in either direction.

That disposes of the rider's arithmetic. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is about whether the completed trip deviated from the route shown at booking, and on the record the answer is no within the meaning of the policy, so the fare as charged stands and nothing is refunded.

THE THRESHOLD. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement and sets two tests that must BOTH pass: the excess must be greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the booking-time optimal. The trace (EV-GPS-09112, weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km of 11.5 km; the booking-time optimal on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09112, weight 1.0) is 10.0 km. The excess is 1.5 km, which clears the 0.8 km absolute limb but is 15.0% of optimal, short of the 20% limb. Because one establishment test fails, POL-RD-01 states there is no deviation and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's submission that the trip was '1.5 km longer' is factually right and is accepted on the measurement; it does not clear the policy threshold, and that is the ground of this ruling.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE IT. (1) The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum inter-fix gap 0.0 s, admissibility COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-RD-07 limbs (a)–(c) are not engaged, the 1.5 km is not a sampling artefact, and the no-corroboration escalation in POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered. Both advocates' claims on this point are accepted. (2) The baseline is 10.0 km and nothing shifts it: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 has no re-quote to apply, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. (3) POL-RD-04 gives the driver no exoneration and takes nothing from the rider either: the only chat message (EV-CHAT-09112) is the rider's own mid-trip remark, it names no place or road and carries a null waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run on this record. (4) The one refund route that survives a failed POL-RD-01 test — billing integrity under POL-RD-09(4) — is closed: no ERP gantry is charged (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge is applied on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. (5) POL-RD-06 is not engaged: 1.5 km / 15.0% is neither greater than 50% nor greater than 8.0 km, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation, and the driver's citable 90-day counters (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 610) show no pattern in any event.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. The rider's arithmetic claim (recomputed_fare 17.70, refund 1.69 rounded up to 1.70, PARTIAL_REFUND) is accepted as arithmetic but not reached, because it is conditional on a deviation being established and none is. The rider's alternative request — that the contested SGD 1.69 be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than left standing — is not granted. A request is not a trigger: POL-RD-01's own terms direct NO_ACTION where a threshold limb fails, and no enumerated POL-RD-10 trigger fires. Trace not impaired (no (3)); trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown and the trace's first fix matches started_at, so no (2); no timestamp conflict, no (4); no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact, because no closure or other exoneration was asserted and the absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09112-01 (weight 0.0) merely confirms POL-RD-03 has nothing to run on, so no (5); no charge line lacks a counterpart, no (8); the refund does not exceed SGD 150.00 or charged_total, no (6); and this is not two sides with contradictory evidence of comparable strength — the rider herself concedes the threshold is not met, no (7). The driver's counter-statement ('ordinary through roads, no additional stop') carries no weight multiplier and no clause in this category names a counterparty statement as its test, so it neither adds nor detracts; the outcome does not depend on it. The profile fields the rider correctly flagged as context-only (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) were not used as a ground of decision by either side, and POL-GEN-01 forbids it.

CONFIDENCE AND OUTCOME. The deciding facts — the trace distance and the booking-time optimal — are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-09112, EV-TRIP-09112), so confidence is not capped below the platform floor and no escalation arises under POL-GEN-02 or POL-RD-10(1). EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and can carry no fact; its absence is noted and changes nothing, since the threshold fails on the unimpaired trace regardless. Ruling: NO_ACTION. fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) are left as they are; the contested SGD 1.69 is neither refunded nor held.

To both parties. The question is whether the SGD 1.69 the rider asks for should be refunded for a trip that ran longer than the booking-time route. It should not, and the charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

Why the deviation is not established. Under POL-RD-01 a route deviation exists only when the excess distance is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal route AND greater than 0.8 km. The two limbs are conjunctive, not alternative, and the clause states that if either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The governing figure is the GPS trace's trace_distance_km of 11.5 km; the trip record's actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booking-time optimal of 10.0 km the excess is 1.5 km. The absolute limb is met (1.5 km > 0.8 km), but the percentage limb is not: 1.5 km is 15.0% of 10.0 km, five points short of the 20% gate. Because both tests must pass, no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION. The rider is right that the extra 1.5 km is real and was driven; the policy simply does not make an excess of that size refundable.

The rider's fare arithmetic is rejected, not because the sums are wrong but because the condition precedent is missing. POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and none is. For the record, had it run, the figures the rider uses are correct: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.0 km + 0.28 x 20.0 min) x surge 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (the only artifact carrying that field), + 0.80 platform fee = recomputed_fare 17.70; charged_total 19.39 less 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to SGD 1.70. That clause is simply never reached.

No escalation. POL-RD-07 is not engaged: the trace carries 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) does not apply. POL-RD-10(1) does not apply, my confidence being well above the 0.70 floor. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-09112), and no timestamps disagree, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not apply. The rider's alternative request that the SGD 1.69 be held under POL-RD-10 is therefore declined: the record is complete on the very question that decides this case, and a claim that fails its own materiality gate is a failure of the claim, not a data failure.

No billing-integrity refund. POL-RD-09(4) is the one refund route that survives a failed threshold test, and it is closed here: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, and no airport surcharge was applied on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom line to refund. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and can carry no fact; its absence is citable but excuses nothing and proves nothing, and since no party asserted a closure, POL-RD-03 simply does not need to run.

No driver compensation. POL-RD-04's compensation limb applies where the rider was billed for less distance than the trace records by more than 1.0 km; here the fare was billed at 11.5 km, matching the trace exactly, so the driver is fully paid and there is no unbilled distance. The driver's account that he stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop cites no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08, but nothing in this ruling turns on it, and the same is true of the chat log, which contains one mid-trip rider remark, names no road or place and carries a null waypoint_hint.

No conduct referral. POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, and a 15.0% / 1.5 km excess is neither greater than 50% of optimal nor greater than 8.0 km. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, far below the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test. The rider's profile counters deviation_claims_60d 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0 do not engage the POL-RD-08 extra-corroboration requirement. The remaining profile counters on both sides are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were given no weight.

Confidence. The deciding fact is carried by the GPS trace and by the trip record's booking-time optimal figure, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; no artifact below full weight carries the finding. Ruling: NO_ACTION, the SGD 1.69 charge standing as billed.
